content:
noah: Quick note — onboarding generator sample leaks goroutines when user hits ctrl-c. Found while testing the flash tutorial.

tess: ack. which sample? the quickstart generator one?

noah: yes. the example does `go readLoop(stream.Chan())` and never calls stream.Close(). On SIGINT the main returns but the goroutine keeps running reading from an open channel.

leo: can you paste the exact snippet that causes it?

noah: minimal repro we used:
```go
func main() {
  // demo uses Background for simplicity (BAD)
  ctx := context.Background()
  gen := sdk.NewGenerator(nil)
  s, _ := gen.Stream(ctx, &Request{Prompt: "hi"})
  go func() {
    for tok := range s.Chan() {
      fmt.Print(tok)
    }
  }()
  // main exits, goroutine still alive
}
```

rahul: yeah that'll stick. most users paste these into docker containers or systemd services and never see graceful shutdown.

noah: also saw a related issue when auth refresh fires mid-stream: the client retries handshake but the old stream's reader stays attached and logs show duplicate "handshake start" lines.

leo: hmm, sounds like the retry path doesn't cancel the previous internal context before re-dial. we should cancel first, wait for teardown, then start a new handshake.

tess: proposal: change Stream signature to return a StreamCloser that embeds Cancel() and Chan(), and ensure Stream.Close() cancels an internal ctx. Example API idea:
```go
type StreamCloser interface {
  Chan() <-chan string
  Close() error // cancels internal ctx and closes channel
}
func (g *Generator) Stream(ctx context.Context, req *Request) (StreamCloser, error)
```
Then samples can defer stream.Close() and use signal.NotifyContext in main.

noah: +1. also update onboarding examples to show signal.NotifyContext so people don't start with Background. tiny snippet to recommend:
```go
ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt)
defer stop()
stream, _ := gen.Stream(ctx, req)
// use for/select with ctx.Done() and <-stream.Chan()
```

rahul: I'll take the runtime change for cancel-on-reconnect. leo, can you own the sample updates? tess, can you add a 1-min smoketest that runs the sample and sends SIGINT and then checks `go test`'s goroutine count?

leo: yep. will swap examples and add small README note on auth retry semantics: "Stream may reconnect on auth refresh; callers should call Close() to cancel previous stream."

ci-bot: Created PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/pull/4150 — generator stream Close() + sample updates + SIGINT smoketest. CI: pending.

tess: fyi the smoketest uses a short container and `go test -run TestSampleSIGINT` which asserts no extra goroutines after shutdown. kept it lightweight.

noah: thanks all. can we also put a short paragraph in the Go SDK README: "Don't use context.Background() in examples; prefer signal.NotifyContext or pass caller ctx". New users keep tripping on this.

leo: agreed. i'll add that to PR. rahul: ping when the runtime unit test for cancel-on-reconnect is green so we can merge.

rahul: on it. will add regression test for auth refresh handshake race.

noah: awesome. small DX win, big reduce in noise for support. :party_parrot:
